# `bulk-edit` commands

## `bulk-edit apply`

Apply a previewed grid edit: one ordinary update per record carrying the version the preview read, each its own audit event, all one batch. A record someone changed meanwhile merges when they changed other fields, and is refused (conflict, naming who and when) when they changed the same one; the rest go on (all or nothing undoes them instead). Returns each record's outcome. Example: {"run": "01J..."}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | bulk-edit |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bulk-edit.apply` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bulk-edit apply 01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BE --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Fixture prices up 5 percent" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bulk-edit apply", "input": {"run": "01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BE"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | `RUN` | string | yes | no | — | The grid edit (from `bulk-edit preview`).; minimum length 26; maximum length 26 |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |

| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bulk-edit.apply`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |

### Output

| JSON field | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | object[string, any] | yes | no | — | The edit: id, kind, state, label, atomic, reason, who and when, its batch (state, reversible, first blocker). |
| `counts` | object[string, integer] | yes | no | — | selected, change, refused, unchanged; after apply also updated, merged, conflict, not_run. |
| `totals` | object[string, any] | yes | no | — | Per money column: the sum before and after over the records that change (exact, in the currency). |
| `rows` | array[object[string, any]] | yes | no | — | The diff, per record: seq, record, label, version, status, changes [{field, before, after}], the refusal at preview, and the outcome at apply (merged_over, version_after). |
| `next_cursor` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | Pass as `cursor` for more rows. |
| `skipped` | array[object[string, any]] | no | no | [] | After a reversal with skip_changed: the records left because they were edited again since. |

## `bulk-edit grid`

The records a selection holds (the list's query filter, search text or named records) with the chosen columns' current values, as the grid shows them. Example: {"kind": "customer", "filter": ["terms=Net 30"], "columns": ["terms_id", "credit_limit"]}.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | bulk-edit |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bulk-edit.grid` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bulk-edit grid customer --columns '["terms_id","credit_limit"]' --limit 200 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json

```

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `filter` | `--filter` | array[string] | no | no | [] | The list's own `query` filters (`customer query --help`), e.g. ["category_id=Fixtures"]. |
| `query` | `--query` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Search text, as the list's `query` takes it. |

| `limit` | `--limit` | integer | no | no | 2000 | Most records to return.; minimum 1; maximum 5000 |

## `bulk-edit preview`

Preview a grid edit of many records of one list (customer, vendor, item, account), changing nothing in the books: pick records by the list's own query `filter`, `query` text or named `records`; give cell `changes`, a `paste`d block and column `operations` (set, clear, copy_down, replace, add, multiply, percent, set_from; a computed amount rounds half-up to the currency's places or to `round`). Returns the diff (each record's fields before and after), money totals before and after, and each record its update would refuse, with the command's code. Then `bulk-edit apply`. Before applying an edit that sets how the business works from now on (new terms or prices), show its exact diff and totals to your principal once. Example: {"kind": "item", "filter": ["category=Fixtures"], "operations": [{"op": "percent", "field": "price", "by": "5", "round": "0.05"}]}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | bulk-edit |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bulk-edit.preview` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bulk-edit preview item --query Fixture --operations '[{"op": "percent", "field": "price", "by": "5", "round": "0.05"}]' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Fixture prices up 5 percent" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bulk-edit preview", "input": {"kind": "item", "query": "Fixture", "operations": [{"op": "percent", "field": "price", "by": "5", "round": "0.05"}]}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `filter` | `--filter` | array[string] | no | no | [] | The list's own `query` filters (`customer query --help`), e.g. ["category_id=Fixtures"]. |
| `query` | `--query` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Search text, as the list's `query` takes it. |
| `include_inactive` | `--include-inactive` | boolean | no | no | false | Include inactive records. |
| `records` | `--records` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Exactly these records (id or full name; an account's number), in this order, instead of a filter. |
| `kind` | `KIND` | literal["customer", "vendor", "item", "account"] | yes | no | — | customer, vendor, item or account. |
| `changes[].record` | inside `--changes` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | Record id or full name (an account's number).; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `changes[].field` | inside `--changes` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | Column, as `bulk-edit columns` names it.; minimum length 1; maximum length 120 |
| `changes[].value` | inside `--changes` JSON array | any | no | no | null | New value as typed ("12.50", "Net 30", true); null or "" clears it. |
| `paste` | `--paste` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Cells pasted from a spreadsheet (tab text). With a header row, columns match by name or label and a Name column picks the record; without one, rows fill the selection in order over `paste_columns`. |
| `paste_columns` | `--paste-columns` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | The columns a header-less paste fills, left to right (default: the grid's columns). |
| `operations[].op` | inside `--operations` JSON array | literal["set", "clear", "copy_down", "replace", "add", "multiply", "percent", "set_from"] | yes | no | — | set: one value on every selected record; clear; copy_down: the first record's value on the rest; replace: `find` with `replace` in text; add: `by` to a number; multiply: by `by`; percent: up (or down, negative) by `by` percent; set_from: copy column `from` of the same record. |
| `operations[].field` | inside `--operations` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | Column the operation changes.; minimum length 1; maximum length 120 |
| `operations[].value` | inside `--operations` JSON array | any | no | no | null | For set. |
| `operations[].by` | inside `--operations` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | For add, multiply and percent: an exact decimal ("5"). |
| `operations[].round` | inside `--operations` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Round add, multiply and percent results half-up to this step ("0.05"); default the currency's places for money, a whole number for a count, six places for other decimals. |
| `operations[].find` | inside `--operations` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | For replace: the text to find (case-sensitive). |
| `operations[].replace` | inside `--operations` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | For replace: what it becomes ("" deletes it). |
| `operations[].from_` | inside `--operations` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | For set_from: the column to copy. |
| `atomic` | `--atomic` | boolean | no | no | false | All or nothing: refused at preview if any record is refused, and at apply the first refusal undoes the records already changed. Default: each record stands alone. |

## `bulk-edit reverse`

Undo a grid edit as one unit: every record it changed gets its exact prior values back through its update. Refused (E_BATCH_BLOCKED), naming each record and who changed it when, if any was edited again since; `skip_changed` restores the rest and leaves those (reversed_partly). --dry-run shows the plan and a fingerprint. Example: {"run": "01J..."}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | bulk-edit |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bulk-edit.reverse` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bulk-edit reverse 01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BE --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Wrong category repriced" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bulk-edit reverse", "input": {"run": "01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BE"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | `RUN` | string | yes | no | — | The grid edit (from `bulk-edit preview`).; minimum length 26; maximum length 26 |
| `skip_changed` | `--skip-changed` | boolean | no | no | false | Reverse every record except those edited again since (they are left as they are and listed; the batch is then reversed_partly). Without it, one such record refuses the whole reversal, naming it. |
| `fingerprint` | `--fingerprint` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The `fingerprint` a dry run returned; the reversal is refused if the batch changed since. |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bulk-edit.reverse`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |

### Output

| JSON field | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | string | yes | no | — | The grid edit. |
| `batch` | object[string, any] | yes | no | — | Its batch after this call. |
| `state` | string | yes | no | — | live (dry run), reversed or reversed_partly. |
| `reversed_now` | integer | yes | no | — | Records restored by this call. |
| `steps` | array[object[string, any]] | yes | no | — | The plan: per record, the update that restores it. |
| `blockers` | array[object[string, any]] | yes | no | — | What blocks the reversal (empty when it can run). |
| `skipped` | array[object[string, any]] | yes | no | — | Records edited again since, left as they are (only with skip_changed), each naming who and when. |
| `fingerprint` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | Pass to the real reversal so it refuses if the batch changed since. |
| `reversal_batch` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | The batch recording the reversal, once begun. |
| `event_id` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | Audit event that finished the reversal. |

Example JSON output:

```json
{
  "batch": {},
  "blockers": [],
  "event_id": null,
  "fingerprint": null,
  "reversal_batch": null,
  "reversed_now": 1,
  "run": "value",
  "skipped": [],
  "state": "value",
  "steps": []
}
```

### Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_BATCH_BLOCKED` | The batch cannot be reversed now; the details name each blocker and what clears it. |
| `E_COMPANY_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one company matches; use the id or Organization/Company. |

| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |

| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |

| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
